At PetZone Mahalaxmi Veterinary Clinic, we are dedicated to the health and well-being of your beloved pets. Knowing when to seek immediate veterinary attention can make all the difference in emergency situations. Here are some critical warning signs that indicate your pet may require urgent care:

1. **Difficulty Breathing**: Labored breathing is a significant red flag. It may indicate respiratory distress and needs immediate medical evaluation.

2. **Sudden Lethargy**: If your pet suddenly becomes unusually tired or inactive, it could be a sign of a serious underlying condition.

3. **Refusal to Eat for More Than 24 Hours**: A sudden loss of appetite, especially when prolonged, can indicate different health threats.

4. **Seizures**: Whether single or multiple, seizures are a medical emergency requiring prompt attention.

5. **Bloating**: Noticeable swelling in the abdomen can signal an emergency, such as gastric dilatation-volvulus in dogs.

6. **Ingestion of Toxins**: If you suspect your pet has ingested something toxic, seek help immediately.

At PetZone Mahalaxmi Veterinary Clinic, our team is always ready to provide expert care when your pet needs it most. Our emergency services are available 24/7, ensuring that no matter the hour, you have access to compassionate and comprehensive veterinary care. 

Don’t wait to address these warning signs — your pet’s health and happiness are our priority. If you notice any of these symptoms, please call us.

featured_reviews.name: Shilpa Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
We would like to share our experience at Tata Small Animal Hospital, which has been a mix of appreciation and concern.

During our first visit, we were extremely satisfied with the services provided. The hospital environment, staff coordination, and overall approach towards small animals were professional, caring, and reassuring. Our experience was pleasant and very helpful, which is why we trusted the hospital for a follow-up consultation as well.

However, during our second visit, we felt somewhat misguided. We consulted Dr. Aishwarya Ramesh and clearly explained the reason for our visit along with our concerns, especially regarding our pet’s ongoing issue of not eating food. While she prescribed certain food and medicines, we were surprised when she advised us to visit her private clinic for the next consultation.

Unfortunately, the private clinic did not meet basic hygiene standards, which made us uncomfortable and raised concerns about continuity of care. As pet parents, we rely on reputed institutions like Tata Small Animal Hospital for transparent, ethical, and consistent guidance.

We have spent nearly ₹8,000 across two visits, yet our pet’s core issue remains unresolved. This leaves us worried about whether future visits to Tata Small Animal Hospital will ensure proper consultation and whether we might again be directed outside the hospital system.

We genuinely respect Tata Small Animal Hospital and hope our feedback is taken constructively. We would appreciate clarity on how patient care continuity is ensured and reassurance that consultations remain within the hospital framework for proper guidance and trust.

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

We lost our 3 year golden retriever and we strongly believe Dr Anoop and his team is primarily responsible for our pup losing her life.

Our pup wasnt eating food for few days towards end of Sep’24. On 1st Oct we called Dr Anoop and he sent his person at home who gave antibiotics injections to my pup and then took blood samples and based on that suggested liver medicines. He said give it for 15-20 days and pup will be fine.

Pup still wasnt eating well after 15 days and we took her to Dr anoop clinic. He saw her and said “your pup is 100% fine, dont worry and take worry off your mind” he asked to continue liver medicine for 1 more week and said its very slight liver thing but not at all serious. He said “sub kutto ka hai, khana nahi khate”. This made us feel even more relaxed that he is experienced and saying / suggesting right and we felt this behaviour of our dog is normal.

After 2-3 days i again wassaped dr anoop that my pup is little less active but reasonable overall, still not eating and she is peeing very yellow. He again said “dont worry”.

After further 2-3 days my pup started puking badly and then we called another doctor at home who suggested to re do the blood tests, ultra sound etc which we immediately did on same day. Next day morning we rushed to pluto clinic where tests were done and they said “admit your pup she is serious and its risk on her life”.

We took her immediately to lowerparel animal hospital and admitted her in ICU but we had to go through the OPD procedure where again we got Dr Anoop who suggested few medications after again casually seeing our pup. He gave medicines for that day in hospital as senior doctors only visit between 10-1pm in that hospital so they would see her only next next day. Same day (29th Oct) after medications of dr anoop my pup started puking heavy blood, peeing blood and pooing blood too. I dont know what medicines were given by him that she couldnt take it at all. She just gave up the next day and died.

Dr Anoop is extremely casual with pets, he doesn’t see the pet carefully what could be the internal problem if a pup is not eating since so many days but makes decision based on her activeness purely which isnt right at all and my pup case is real example. She was hyper in his clinic because she was scared of clinic but he confidently said she is super active and well nothing to worry.

If Dr Anoop had carefully diagnosed my dog she would have been alive now. I would strongly recommended not to visit him as if similar thing happens with your pup you will not be able to forgive yourself.

I am not just blaming Dr Anoop, but i am also said that why did i believed this doc and not take second opinion. It was our first experience and we just blatantly believed his words which was our mistake.

Dr Anoop, pets are special for many, you should ensure you do strictly great job with them. People come to you with trust and hope but you and your team do not treat them or doesn’t diagnose them carefully which in many instances can lead to loss of their lives.
